- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.3), model often underestimates; adjust downward bias, especially if recent price is rising.
- After a sharp spike (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction to prevent overreaction.
- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — reduce initial forecast by 1–2% for such cases.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days of decline after peak), model often fails to recognize it — add a “reversion buffer” to forecast, especially if sentiment is flat or negative.
- When sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from +0.2 to -0.3), model often lags — adjust forecast to reflect sentiment shift within 2–3 days.
